(i) the problem of mining frequent itemsets with a taxonomy is NP-hard in the general case, but it is solvable in polynomial time if the taxonomy has bounded depth; (ii) the problem of identifying frequent itemsets is solvable with a number of crowd questions that is linear in the number of frequent itemsets, and in the size of the taxonomy; and (iii) the problem of finding a concise description of frequent itemsets is NP-hard even if the taxonomy is a tree,
the complexity of mining itemsets from the crowd is determined by the structure of the taxonomy, and that the complexity of the mining problem is not affected by the size of the output itemset.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when the taxonomy is small and the description of the output is concise, the crowd complexity can be low, but the computational complexity can still be high.
, for the most general case, crowd and computational complexities are both exponential in the size of the input taxonomy and in the size of a succinct representation of the output itemset lattice.
, for a given itemset, the crowd can be used to determine whether it is frequent or not by asking a number of questions that is linear in the size of the taxonomy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of a good taxonomy of the itemset domain, it is possible to find the frequent itemsets with a small number of crowd questions, even if the number of itemsets to be considered is exponential in the number of items.
frequent itemset mining with a crowd and a taxonomy can be done in polynomial time in the worst case, and in linear time for a large class of input taxonomies.
frequent itemset mining with taxonomies is a computationally hard problem, but that it can be made efficient with appropriate choices of the taxonomy and the concise description.
